sites.functional_impact_measured: Methotrexate binding and uptake assays in full-length, membrane-anchored construct: minor effects on both binding and uptake (surface_and_function preserved).
sites.rationale: The ledger (PMID 10347183) explicitly names Pro-297 as the insertion site in the external loop between TM7 and TM8. Python lookup confirms residue 297 = P (Pro) and residue 298 = T in the canonical sequence. The topology landmarks place EXTRACELLULAR_4 at 289–307; Pro-297 is 9 residues from the TM7 boundary (288) and 11 residues from TM8 (308), both well above the ≥3-residue minimum. The paper used a full-length, membrane-anchored construct (not a secreted ectodomain), and the HA insertion was functionally validated with only minor effects on methotrexate binding and uptake. insert_after_residue=297 places the tag between P(297) and T(298), mid-loop on the extracellular face. HA epitope tag inserted at Pro-297 in the extracellular loop between TM7 and TM8 (EXTRACELLULAR_4, residues 289–307) of full-length human SLC19A1 fused to C-terminal eGFP; expressed in mammalian cells and tested for [3H]-methotrexate binding and uptake. Minor effects on both binding and uptake were reported. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The hemagglutinin epitope insertion mutants were also tested for their effects on the function of the reduced folate carrier. For these studies, each of the constructs had a carboxyl-terminal fusion of the enhanced green fluorescent protein to monitor and quantitate expression. Insertions into the external loop between transmembrane regions 7 and 8 (Pro-297), the cytoplasmic loop between transmembrane regions 6 and 7 (Ser-225), and near the cytoplasmic amino and carboxyl termini (Pro-20 and Gly-492, respectively) had minor effects on methotrexate binding and uptake.

sites.functional_impact_measured: Methotrexate binding and uptake assays in full-length, membrane-anchored construct: binding preserved but uptake selectively reduced (function_perturbed).
sites.rationale: The ledger (PMID 10347183) explicitly names Pro-427 as the insertion site in the external loop between TM11 and TM12. Python lookup confirms residue 427 = P (Pro) and residue 428 = V in the canonical sequence. The topology landmarks place EXTRACELLULAR_6 at 419–431; Pro-427 is 9 residues from the TM11 boundary (418) and 5 residues from TM12 (432), both above the ≥3-residue minimum. The paper used a full-length, membrane-anchored construct. However, the insertion selectively interfered with uptake (though not binding), so validation_level is function_perturbed. This site is ranked lower than Pro-297 due to the functional perturbation. insert_after_residue=427 places the tag between P(427) and V(428) on the extracellular face. HA epitope tag inserted at Pro-427 in the extracellular loop between TM11 and TM12 (EXTRACELLULAR_6, residues 419–431) of full-length human SLC19A1 fused to C-terminal eGFP; expressed in mammalian cells and tested for [3H]-methotrexate binding and uptake. The insertion selectively interfered with uptake but not binding, indicating partial functional perturbation. [validation: function_perturbed; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The insertion into the cytoplasmic loop between transmembrane regions 10 and 11 (Gln-385) greatly reduced both binding and uptake of methotrexate, whereas the insertion into the external loop between transmembrane regions 11 and 12 (Pro-427) selectively interfered with uptake but not binding.
